ts-node hooks into Node's module loading and by default runs the real TypeScript compiler, so it type-checks while it runs (slow, unless you set transpile-only). tsx uses esbuild to just strip types, so it's much faster and handles ESM and CJS interop, but it does not type-check. That means scripts run through tsx still need `tsc --noEmit` somewhere to catch type errors.
Action: none needed for the question; I still haven't run an install for the tsx change, so run it from the repo root before committing.

I'll make the csv download name `invoices-<org slug>.csv`, e.g. invoices-northwind.csv. The slug needs to be filename-safe, so I'll use the org's slug field if it has one, otherwise slugify the name.
Action: find where the csv Content-Disposition filename is built, add the org slug, fall back to invoices.csv if the slug is empty, and update the export test that asserts the filename.

In production Next.js hides server error messages and gives the client an `error.digest` instead, and Sentry only captures that if we attach it explicitly. A likely fix is to pass the digest as a tag or extra context when global-error.tsx calls Sentry.
Action: open app/global-error.tsx, check how it reports to Sentry, add `error.digest` as a tag, check no beforeSend filter strips it, and verify with a thrown test error.

The trace alone doesn't show why (a different api response shape or a missing field for some invoices), so I'd confirm that.
Action: read InvoiceLineItems.tsx around line 24 and how InvoiceDetail gets the data, find which payload lacks the field, fix it at the source plus a safe default, and add a regression test.

`docker compose up -d` creates any missing containers, networks and volumes, recreates containers whose config or image changed, and starts them in the background. `docker compose start` only starts containers that already exist and are stopped, with no creation and no pickup of compose file changes.
Action: none needed; use `up -d` after editing compose files.

There's a real difference. `structuredClone` keeps Dates as Dates and handles Map, Set, typed arrays, undefined, NaN, BigInt and circular references, but throws on functions and DOM nodes. The JSON trick turns Dates into strings, drops undefined and functions, and throws on circular references and BigInt, so use `structuredClone` unless you specifically want a JSON-safe copy.
Action: none needed.
